claims.text: Replacing Mn with Al in CrFeCoNiX promotes formation of an alumina-rich interfacial sublayer during high-temperature oxidation.
The alumina-rich sublayer is more coherent and resistant to cracking and spallation than the oxide formed on CrFeCoNiMn.
Alumina has lower oxygen diffusivity than the relevant oxide scale on CrFeCoNiMn.
Alumina has a better thermal-expansion match with the CrFeCoNiAl substrate than the Mn-containing oxide scale has with CrFeCoNiMn.
Lower oxygen diffusivity inhibits rapid oxide growth.
Improved thermal-expansion matching reduces oxide-scale interfacial stresses.
Al in CrFeCoNiAl preferentially oxidizes to form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 sublayer.
A continuous alumina sublayer limits oxygen ingress into CrFeCoNiAl.
Mn in CrFeCoNiMn forms oxides that are less stable than the proposed alumina sublayer.
Mn oxidation produces volatile products under the stated high-temperature conditions.
Rapid growth, volatile oxidation products, and higher interfacial stresses make the Mn-containing scale prone to cracking and spallation.
Under identical high-temperature oxidative exposure, CrFeCoNiAl will have slower oxide growth than CrFeCoNiMn.
Under identical high-temperature oxidative exposure, CrFeCoNiAl will show less cracking and spallation and greater scale adherence than CrFeCoNiMn.
CrFeCoNiMn forms an unstable oxide layer that cracks and spalls under the proposed control conditions.
The hypothesis applies above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres during extended high-temperature service.
The proposed comparison concerns CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiMn in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
Identical processing will ensure comparable microstructures between the chemically different alloys.
Microstructural variations may influence oxide-scale integrity.
